blindReviewDeclaration: Fresh v2s-rooted independent-subagent review. I first derived counterexamples from the authorization, canonical operation registry, current topology/read-policy and checker sources, then read the design and author requirements to test those counterexamples. No author intake/disposition was read, and no dynamic resource was started.

riskClasses: 68 M1 generated-binding and command transaction reachability
fresh request-local fact attribution without cache or second-origin bypass
task-read/protocol-exemption fidelity without a universal numeric cap
same-basis report comparison and final technical-acceptance authority

expectedBehavior: Every current and future canonical operation is admitted only by an independently authoritative exact source-anchor denominator, never by a matrix row that can authorize its own production path.
All 68 M1 HTTP entries reach their declared generated binding, while command paths retain one REQUIRED origin and owner recheck before receipt replay.
Task reads and five protocol/content exemptions remain shape-specific; no universal numeric ceiling is introduced.
The comparison is immutable, same-basis and UPDATE-conserving, and final technical acceptance is never reported as browser L2 or UAT.

findings.title: The proposed shape matrix self-authorizes its production source surface, so it cannot fail closed against a new bypass.
findings.evidence: The design's 'Fixed denominator and source of truth' makes the new matrix own edge/http/transaction source anchors, and lines 225-231 admit all Java paths only from anchors derived from that same future matrix. Current contracts/registry/operation-handler-bindings.json has no sourceAnchor or adapterSourcePath on any operation (independent jq recomputation), so there is no pre-existing immutable source-anchor denominator to constrain the new matrix. A change can add a new operation row or replace a row's anchor with an arbitrary controller/owner helper, then change that now-'admitted' source; exact matrix closure still passes. This violates the design's claimed no-broad-admission and the routed redline PER_OPERATION_DESIGN_CONTRACT requirement for a finite edge/coordinator/owner call chain before implementation.
findings.risk: The control can prove 196 registry rows exist while silently allowing a direct adapter, extra transaction origin, cache, or cross-owner read in a self-declared path. It therefore does not deliver the requested permanent future-operation prevention.
findings.disposition: Minimal correction: add an independently generated, hash-bound operation-to-edge/coordinator/owner source-inventory as the source denominator before the shape matrix; matrix anchors may only reference that inventory and its exact-set generator must reject additions, substitutions and orphaned paths. Declare that inventory and its generator/checker as BPF-U01 source surfaces, then make BPF-U02–U05 consume—not extend—the admission authority.

findings.title: BPF-U05 assumes an existing task-read control that currently fails before its self-test can establish the intended baseline.
findings.evidence: Running scripts/check/backend-performance-read-budget --self-test in this review returns BP_U05_READ_SOURCE_ANCHOR_MISSING:apps/backend/catering-business-server/src/main/java/com/catering/v2s/app/edge/operations/context/OperationsWorkspaceUserController.java#revoke. scripts/generate/task-read-surface-policy.mjs:22-27 hard-codes that command anchor, but OperationsWorkspaceUserController currently exposes groupRevoke, regionRevoke, projectRevoke, headCompanyRevoke and storeRevoke; it has no revoke method. The design only says the task-read checker 'gains shape-row joins and explanation completeness' and its BPF-U05 change surfaces do not identify this stale command-anchor repair or require restoring the existing baseline before extension.
findings.risk: A package that is required to keep existing gates green starts from a broken task-read source check. Extending it can mask the failed command/read separation rather than prove the 78 reads and five exemptions are safely closed.
findings.disposition: Minimal correction: make the stale workspace-command-anchor family an explicit BPF-U05 precondition and source repair, with the five exact revoke entry points (or a deliberate finite replacement) declared and a red mutation for each lost anchor. Require the existing checker clean result before adding shape joins, then retain its current command/read separation control.

findings.title: The verification sequence authorizes the wrong execution class by placing browser L2 in the final technical-acceptance lifecycle.
findings.evidence: The design at lines 235-238 says a separately authorized managed lifecycle may create evidence, compare seed reports, 'run browser L2' and report business/cleanup. The controlling final-closure authorization explicitly says its managed workload is technical verification, 'not DEV product acceptance, browser L2, UAT or deployment' (doc/decisions/2026-08-10-v2s-backend-performance-final-closure-authorization.md, Boundaries). The design-only authorization also excludes browser L2. The routed EXECUTION_EVIDENCE_TAXONOMY redline requires these execution classes to remain separately declared and never mutually upgradeable.
findings.risk: Later implementation can treat the performance runner's evidence lifecycle as permission or a prerequisite for browser L2, confusing final HTTP/measurement evidence with a Journey-level business result and its separate cleanup scope.
findings.disposition: Minimal correction: remove browser L2 from BPF-U06 and the final-closure sequence. State that this package can only produce managed technical HTTP/performance evidence and its own cleanup; any browser L2 is a separately authorized Journey package with a distinct manifest, denominator, business oracle and cleanup evidence.

findings.title: The proposed shape vocabulary preserves the important non-uniform counterexamples.
findings.evidence: Independent registry counts are 196 total, 113 COMMAND and 83 READ; command topology is 68/20/9/7/9 and task-read policy is 78 TASK_READ plus five PROTOCOL_READ_EXEMPT rows. The design explicitly retains two NO_CONTENT M1 commands, five exemption evidence reasons, owner-local folds, required readback and above-floor task-read explanations. Its component model therefore does not itself impose the prohibited global numeric ceiling.
findings.risk: This is not sufficient to prevent the three major scope/control defects above.
findings.disposition: Retain this closed shape vocabulary and the no-global-cap rule when correcting the blocking findings.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: The requested permanent discipline is correctly aimed at preventing repeated database work without deleting owner authorization, receipts, CAS, audit or required readback. The present self-authorizing source map does not solve that future-bypass problem.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: A finite generated source-inventory derived from the canonical route/handler registries is smaller and safer than inventing a broad call-graph framework or a global SQL threshold. Repairing the existing stale anchor before extending its checker is also smaller than replacing the task-read control.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The proposed six-unit package is proportionate only after it stops matrix self-admission and keeps the final performance runner within its technical execution class. Those corrections add bounded registry/control work rather than infrastructure or a cache/query bus.
solutionReasonableness.verdict: NO_GO until the three confirmed major defects are repaired and independently re-reviewed.

conclusion.summary: The 196-row model correctly preserves no-content, protocol, task-read and owner-local counterexamples, but the design cannot yet be admitted. Its new matrix would authorize its own production paths, the task-read checker it extends currently fails on a stale command anchor, and the final sequence incorrectly includes browser L2 in a technical-acceptance package. Static self-tests that did pass were sql-merge coverage, evidence snapshot and implementation-design-granularity; read-budget did not pass.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: This independent DESIGN Round 1 verdict authorizes no production or script change, runtime, DEV, reset, seed, Testcontainers, tunnel, browser L2, UAT, deployment, measured performance-success claim or additional adversarial round. The author may only prepare bounded design corrections within the existing design-only authorization, then request DESIGN Round 2, the cycle's final independent review.
